statement: Writes are fenced by partition epoch at the partition boundary: the QUERY payload carries expectedPartitionVersion and handleRemoteQuery rejects on mismatch with a typed stale-epoch outcome, and missing descriptor-epoch evidence defers pre-cutover or fails closed post-cutover instead of skipping validation — a restart can never silently disable mirroring or accept writes against a withdrawn epoch. doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/write-path-epoch-fencing.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — payload-carriage, mismatch-rejection, pre-cutover-defer, and post-cutover-fail-closed receipts all passing.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Epoch evidence must never fail open: a cold-cache descriptor-epoch gap defers (pre-cutover) or fails closed (post-cutover) instead of skipping validation; the partition-descriptor-epoch contract module is already fail-closed and stays the decision owner — callers stop swallowing its absence.

handleRemoteQuery rejects a write whose expectedPartitionVersion mismatches the locally authoritative epoch with a typed stale-epoch outcome routed back through the executor's retry machinery; a withdrawn-epoch write must never be applied.
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding fencing/rejection mechanism is reverted while the rest of the change remains.

The oracle evidence files must be written by a deterministic evidence harness that re-runs the recorded proof commands (focused test files, red-on-revert checks) at quest terminal; no hand-authored metric values.
